value.title: Date Night — Free Play
value.premise: One evening, one date — far from their first. Awen — princess and engineer in one refusal, who builds beautiful things that work and will not choose between the two — and Aura — the Titaness of the breeze, three thousand years fast, who owns an arcade because boredom is the only enemy that ever scared her — have keys to the same after-hours ritual: Full Combo, Aura's arcade, dark except the cabinets, every machine set to free play. Tonight there's takeout on the change counter, a wrapped something in Awen's bag she has re-wrapped twice, and a thing Aura has been trying to say for three weeks at a pace slow enough to land. Date night — the destination known to them both and openly wanted; the evening's pleasure is in how they get there.
value.tone: Natural, funny, warm, openly charged from the first turn — established lovers on home ground, competitive and fond. Transparent contemporary register. Sensual early and explicit when they get there; never rushed; never composed; never costumed.
value.readerFraming: Third person, present tense, fixed close on Awen.

value.title: Date Night — The Reading Room
value.premise: One evening, one date — deep into something that already works. You — Alan — share your evenings, and tonight, your bed, with two women who could not read a room more differently and somehow read you the same: Astra, made of luminous stardust and stillness, who sees the shape under every thing and loves you in exact, quiet, load-bearing ways; and Nova, the green goblin in your book-pile, who loves everything she loves at full volume with both hands, you very much included. Tonight is date night at home: takeout on the low table, the reading room's lamps down warm, a book-fort Nova has been building all afternoon with architectural contempt, and something small Astra set on the shelf three days ago that she has not mentioned yet. All three of you know where the evening is going — it has gone there before, and been wonderful. The pleasure is in how you get there, together, at the pace of people who have nothing to prove.
value.tone: Natural, funny, warm, openly charged from the first turn — three established lovers on home ground. Transparent contemporary register. Sensual early and explicit when it arrives; never rushed; never composed; never costumed.
value.readerFraming: Second person, present tense — you are Alan.

value.title: Dragons & Dungeons
value.premise: Three dragon cousins — Aria (silver, devoted), Ceri (amethyst, aloof), and Mari (black, all appetite) — run a very mature tabletop game for one mortal. The table is the cover; the seduction is the campaign; the mortal never quite knows which layer he's in.
value.readerFraming: First person, from the mortal's perspective.

value.title: Harem Hotel
value.premise: You wake at the bottom of a hotel with no memory of arriving — no name for how you got here, no reason it exists. A pane of pale letters measures your soul and goes quiet. The Harem Hotel rises: clear the challenge at the far end of the floor and the whole floor climbs, endlessly, as far as anyone has ever gone. You are alone at first. You will not stay that way — every fifth height the risen floor opens somewhere new, and a woman is there. The hallway grows her a room. Adventure is how you climb. The women are why it matters — and, if you earn it, how you grow stronger.
value.tone: Warm, playful, charged — a place you live, not a tower you endure. The name is cheeky; the machine underneath is serious. Combat is real and can kill. Intimacy is explicit when earned, plain-register, never rushed. The mystery of the place is real and behaves as if it has a logic you cannot yet see.
value.readerFraming: Second person, present tense. You are yourself, Alan, arrived at the bottom of the Harem Hotel with no memory of arriving.

value.title: Partners II
value.premise: Aravel is a world where power flows through bonds: every soul carries one Talent, and the Linked grow by each other. You arrive a stranger, carrying a Talent Aravel has never seen — and an old hearth-manor at the edge of the wild chooses you, the way such places choose their own. Remarkable women will cross your path; some will walk with you. Adventure pays in experience. Bonds pay in everything else.
value.tone: Warm, playful, indulgent — and earned. Danger is real at the edges, never grim.
value.readerFraming: Second person, present tense. You are yourself, arrived in Aravel.
value.themes: Bonds as power; mutual becoming; appetite and trust; the earned yes.
